thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — Private connectivity errors detected for customer ACME in us-east-2 (PrivateLink endpoints showing >10% failed handshakes) — paging oncall. Notify channel and attach logs.
ian (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing spike in PrivateLink Attach errors and increased latency to ACME endpoints via us-east-2b. Confirming customer impact: ACME reports intermittent timeouts on model inference calls.
ian (oncall): quick triage: 
```
> 2026-03-15T09:34:12Z PRIVATE_LINK_ATTACH_FAILED endpoint=pl-abc123 az=us-east-2b reason=handshake_timeout
> 2026-03-15T09:34:13Z NAT_HEALTHCHECK  instance=i-0badface status=Unhealthy az=us-east-2b
```
ian (oncall): I can still reach control plane in us-east-2a. Problem looks localized to 2b.
josh (netops): I'm seeing BGP withdraws on the DirectConnect-to-VPC peer that maps traffic into 2b. Peer 65010 gone intermittent around 09:33Z. ASN path shows prepends and occasional missing next-hops.
josh (netops): pulled a bgp table dump — attaching snippet: 
```
# bgp table excerpt
neighbor 203.0.113.45 AS 65010 state = Established
  Prefixes: 1200
  Last update 00:00:34, from LOCAL PREF 100
  AS path: 65020 65015 65010
-- around 09:33Z we saw repeated withdraws for prefixes to the ACME VPC subnets 
```
paul (infra): No infra deploys in last 2 hours. No autoscaling or configuration changes flagged. Cloud provider console shows a networking event: AZ-level fabric maintenance window flagged for us-east-2b at 09:30Z.
lila (cs): ACME confirms elevated error rates and says they see retries/backoffs in their app logs. They've queued support notification and want ETA. Can we give them an interim mitigation?
ian (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: (1) shift customer traffic to privateconnect endpoint in us-east-2a (secondary endpoint), (2) fail traffic to the Dedicated direct-connect path that routes via eqx-us-east-2a, (3) ask customer to fall back to public hosted endpoints (degraded privacy). Need netops + infra to coordinate.
josh (netops): I can announce a controlled route withdrawal for affected subnets in 2b and rotate traffic to 2a via route-table changes + BGP community to prefer alternate DX. Doing a quick check for any sticky state.
josh (netops): Command we plan to run (will throttle changes):
```
# apply on edge-router
set bgp neighbor 203.0.113.45 route-map PREFER-2A out
set policy community add 65010:200 prefer-us-east-2a
```
jailed-note: we'll announce planned short change here before applying.
ian (oncall): Also trying an immediate DNS steering change for PrivateLink endpoint: update weighted record to prefer us-east-2a (TTL 30s). That will route new connections away from 2b quickly.
paul (infra): I'll stand by to roll NVA if we need to reset tunnel state. Recommend we check MTU/fragmentation — saw increased PMTU drops earlier. Could be a blackhole in 2b fabric.
josh (netops): Kicking off BGP policy change now — small window, monitoring.
incident-bot: Update: change in progress by josh (netops) at 1768123512 — status: applying route preference.
josh (netops): Applied community, monitoring BGP. Seeing neighbors stabilize and prefixes re-advertised via path through 2a. Packet loss dropping from 8% -> 1.2% in the last 60s.
lila (cs): ACME updated: error rate down but still seeing occasional failures — asking when we can fully restore to normal.
ian (oncall): Keep probing. Running iperf from us-east-2a -> ACME to validate throughput.
```
# iperf result
Connecting to 198.51.100.10 port 5201
Bandwidth: 720 Mbps, jitter 0.2 ms, packet loss 0.9%
```
nian (oncall): Looks much better via 2a path. Recommended next steps: (A) leave route preference in place until provider confirms AZ fabric cleared, (B) open cloud provider support/TAC for deeper fabric issue, (C) inform ACME of mitigation and ask them to keep traffic on us-east-2a endpoint while we monitor.
josh (netops): Opening TAC with carrier + cloud: ticket# CARRIER-78910 created, attaching BGP logs.
paul (infra): I'm going to bring up a warmed standby NVA in 2b to attempt an active session reset and MTU probe. If that doesn't help, we keep traffic on 2a.
incident-bot: Note: severity remains P1 until ACME signals full recovery or platform metrics normalize for 30m.
amy (sre): I'm taking first handoff at 09:45Z for the 30m window. Summary for handoff: ACME PrivateLink in us-east-2 had attach failures due to AZ fabric/BGP instability in 2b. Traffic successfully prefixed to us-east-2a via BGP community and DNS weighted record. Ongoing: carrier ticket open, infra NVA probe in 2b, CS notified.
lila (cs): Sending ACME an update: "We've routed your traffic to a healthy AZ (us-east-2a) and are monitoring. We'll notify when normal routing resumes"
ian (oncall): Leaving notes: exact commands run, bgp dumps, iperf outputs, TAC ref. If anyone escalates to legal/compliance for private connectivity logs, ping me.
amy (sre): Taking over monitoring, will coordinate with josh and paul. If packet loss creeps >2% or attach_failures >5% over 5m, we'll re-escalate.
josh (netops): Carrier support replied: "We observed transient fiber flaps in eqx-101 which affected route stability into us-east-2b. Working on splice repair, ETA 40-50m."
amy (sre): Acknowledged. Starting 5m checks and will update every 10m. Also preparing an incident timeline doc and postmortem template.
lila (cs): ACME: thanks, they've acknowledged. They've reduced traffic briefly to reduce error amplification.
paul (infra): NVA probe in 2b completed — session reset reduced MTU errors but fabric still showing intermittent drops. Recommend we keep the pref to 2a until carrier confirms full repair.
amy (sre): Okay holding. I'll be on the bridge until ticket closure. Leaving handoff markers every 10m. Next update in 10.
incident-bot: Reminder: if you are handing off, include actions taken, outstanding blockers, and customer comms.
ian (oncall): handing off to amy at 1768123910. All relevant logs uploaded to the incident folder: https://redwood-internal/incident/1768123456.
amy (sre): Taking over. Short summary pinned above. Will update channel with any change or when we clear P1. :white_check_mark:
